text:
henry: customer reports they cannot edit project settings in Console — Save button is disabled and API calls to PATCH /v1/projects/:id return 403. Happened after they performed a SCIM group rename in Okta earlier today :thinking_face:
maya: thanks — can you paste the user id + project id and a minimal repro curl?
henry: user is maya.j@acme.com, project: proj-0a1b2c. Repro: `curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj-0a1b2c -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' -d '{"settings":{"allow_guest":false}}'` -> 403, body: `{\"error\":\"forbidden\",\"message\":\"insufficient_permissions: update_project\"}`
sara: can you check token scopes for that API key? Also any recent RBAC or org changes?
henry: support-bot shows token scopes: [`projects:read`, `projects:settings:read`]. No `projects:settings:write`. But the user used a delegated service token that should inherit project-admin role. They say they were project admin before the SCIM rename.
maya: FYI I confirmed in Okta the group rename changed group displayName from `acme-project-admins` -> `acme-project-admins-v2`. SCIM mapping should map by group id not name but customer did a full group replace earlier.
sara: that explains the symptom. Likely role binding is keyed to external group id and the rename replaced the group entry (new id). Can you fetch role bindings for proj-0a1b2c? Use internal tool `rbac-cli get-bindings --project proj-0a1b2c` and paste output.
henry: pasted output below (sanitized):
```
[
  {"binding_id":"b-9f1","principal":"okta:group:00g1oldid","role":"project_admin"},
  {"binding_id":"b-5a2","principal":"user:maya.j@acme.com","role":"editor"}
]
```
henry: looks like the binding refers to the old Okta group id `00g1oldid` which no longer maps to any live group after the sync, so group admins got orphaned.
support-bot: Automated note: detected mismatch between SCIM group ids and RBAC bindings — candidate cause: group-replace + new group id.
maya: is there a safe remediation we can do for the customer without writing a migration script?
sara: short term workaround: add maya.j@acme.com directly to the project with `project_admin` role while we repair the binding. Command: `rbac-cli add-member --project proj-0a1b2c --member maya.j@acme.com --role project_admin`
eng-oncall: longer term we should detect when SCIM group replace occurs and backfill bindings if same displayName exists but group id changed — but need sign-off. For now, henry, run the workaround and request a SCIM resync from the IdP (incremental resync might not recreate the old id).
henry: applied workaround, user can now save settings. Customer will run an IdP resync and share logs. I've flagged this as P2 and will escalate to eng to discuss auto-backfill.
eng-oncall: investigative notes: probable root cause = Okta group-replace flow created new group with new external id; our role bindings persist against external id. Proposed fixes:
- Add detection for displayName collisions on SCIM sync and emit an alert and optional auto-attach-backfill (safe only if displayName match + small member diff).
- Add admin UI action to reconcile orphaned bindings by searching for groups with similar names.
sara: thanks. Maya / acme: please confirm once you complete resync. If the resync recreates old id we can just reattach existing binding otherwise we'll provide a migration helper to map old -> new.
maya: resync completed — Okta created a new group id `00g2newid`. Confirmed RBAC still references old id. We prefer not to add all members manually.
henry: starting migration helper: `rbac-cli migrate-group-id --project proj-0a1b2c --from 00g1oldid --to 00g2newid` — ran in dry-run, shows 42 members to rebind. Customer okayed real run.
support-bot: Ran migration helper, updated 42 bindings. Customer confirms settings now editable and API PATCH returns 200 :tada:
henry: closing thread once we ship a follow-up RFC to product to add displayName-based reconciliation and an admin audit for orphaned bindings.
eng-oncall: assigning follow-up ticket INF-1024 to eng-platform. :thumbsup:
